Indian Standard
REQUI REMENTS FOR PACKING OF PESTICIDES
PART III HOUSEHOLD PESTICIDES

O.

FOR E W 0 R D

0.1 This Indian Standard (Part III) was adopted by the Indian Standards l nsritutron on 29 June 1979. after the draft fina lrzed by the Pest Control Sectional Comrmttee had been approved by the Agmcultural and Food Products Division Councrl and the Chemical D,VISion Council. 0.2 Though, by and large, the packing provrsions con lamed in the relevant Indian Standards fOT pesticides, tec hn ic a l and tberr formulations, were adopted hy the Registr auon Oornmntee of the Central Insecticide Board, there were some modifications, which now, with the promulgation of the Insecticides Act, 19h8 have assumed statutory
character. Opportunity has, therefore, been taken to bnng the packmg requirements in alignment WIth those given in the l nsecrrcsdes Act, and

the rules framed thereunder specially in view of availabrhty of new alternative packing materials and advances III technology in thrs field. These, requirements, thus supersede the packing requrre ments of pesticides and their formulations as given III relevant Indian Standards. 0.3 This standard IS being published in parts. This part covers the requirement for packing of household pesticides. The other parts are as follows: Part I Solid pesticides Part II Liquid pesticides Part IV Fumigant. 0.4 The list of Indian Standards relating to packaging referred to in this standard is grven in Appendix A. 0.5 In the preparation of this standard, due con srdera rion has been given to the provISIOns of the Insecticide Act, 1968 and the rules framed thereunder However, this standard i~ subject to latest provisions made thereunder wherever applicable. 3

IS : 8190 ( Part III ) - 1979

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard IS comphed with, the final value. observed or calculated,
expre . . <ing the result of a test or analysis. shall be rounded off in accordance with IS . 2-1960�. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that 01 the specified value in this standard.

I. SCOPE

1.1 ThIS standard (Part III ) covers the requirements for packing of
household pe'ticides.
NOTE Household pestrcides shall be the pes ucrdev approved for reg rs tre uon by Reg-isn-e uon Oom mut ee or the Central Insecucrdes Board from time to time under the Insecticides Act 1968 as such.

2. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
2.1 The household pesticides. unless specified otherwise in Tables 1 and 2 shall be packed in a container in the quantities of 25 ml, 50 ml, 100 rnl , 2\0 ml , 500 ml, I htre, 5 Iitre s, 10 lrtres, 25 lit res and 50 Iitres or 25 g, 50 g, 100 g, 250 g, 500 g, I kg, 5 kg, 10 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg, 2.2 Primary pack contaming up to I kg or I htre of material, shall be � further packed In outer corrugated fibreboard boxes [,<e& IS: 2771 . (Pdrt 1)-1977 ] or wooden cases (se< IS: 1503-1979) wherever they reqUIre rransportanon, 2.3 Glass bottles, wherever allowed, for packmg of liquid pesticides meant fOT household use shall be fUTther packed in outer corrugated fibreboard boxes [St2 IS: 2771 ( Part I )-1975 ] or wooden cases (see IS' 1503-1979) with suitable and adequate cushioning and absorbing material 2.4 The high density polyethylene (HOPE) used in fabrication of HDPE containers or its components shall be of designation HDPE 43 BA having melt flow index ( i,) not more than 1'8 gfJO rnmutes ( see

IS: 7328-1974t ).
2.5 Aluminium used in fabrication of containers shall Grade 19500 of IS : 737-1974!. conform to

�Rules for roundmg off numerical values ( nlJued). tSpecificauon for high denart y polyethylene materials for moulding and extrueron, tSpecification for wrought alurmmum alloys) sheet and strip ( foe general engineerIng purposes) ( Je�"f1d revIsion).

4

IS : 8190 ( Part III ) - 1979

2.6 The trilaminate pouch shall consist of 55/60 g paper, 0'009 rnm alumrmurn foil and 0'0375 mm polyethylene.
2.7 Containers of mild steel and tinplate mayor may not be lacquered internally but shall be lacquered externally to prevent rustmg, If lIthographed, the top and bottom components shall only be lacquered from the outside. 2.8 In case of containers holding solid pesticides, heat sealing of these conta mers, if applicable, shall be such that no powder comes out from seams during normal handhng. Closures wherever provided shall be leak-proo f. 2.9 In case of containers holding liquid pesticides, closures provided shall be such as not to allow any material to leak through them. These shall be pilferproof 2.10 Containers holding 5 litres or more of hquid pesticides shall be provided with a suitable pouring device with each container. 2.11 Double hessian jute bags (s.. IS: 8115-1976), OW tarpaulin lammated jute bags ( see IS : 8 \ 17 -1976) and H DPE woven sacks ( ,u IS: 8069.1979), used for packing pesticrdes, wherever allowed, shall be provided with an Internal loose polyethylene. liner of not less than 0'062 mm thickness and m the form of tubular sheath, bottom sealed. ~ The length and breadth of the loose liner shall be 10 percent and 5 percent more respectively than those of the outer bag.

2.12 The containers shall be of sturdy design and shall conform to
relevant Indian Standards. 2.13 The packing shall also conform to the Tariff Rules in force from time to time for packing of goods falling III the category of materials of low flash point, dangerous or toxic, wherever applicable.

2.14 Except the pesticides as specified in Table 2, the household
pesticides shall be packed in dry and clean containers as described in Table I.

3. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
3.1 The household pesticides ( see 2.14) shall be packed m dry and clean containers as descubed in Table 2.
